summary: Plan and monitor resource-related development activities using practical frameworks and case exercises. Explore the five-day course outline.
lede: Natural resource management in development programs plans and tracks activities affecting land, water, forests, and community resource access. This intermediate course is for development officers, natural resource specialists, and monitoring staff who need to connect resource measures with program outcomes. You will practise analyzing pressures with DPSIR, mapping resource access and stakeholder roles, and setting indicators and mitigation actions that can be reviewed and adapted as evidence changes.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course suits professionals who shape, deliver, or monitor development activities that affect natural resources and community access to them.
prerequisites: Prior experience in development program design, implementation, or monitoring is recommended, along with basic familiarity with natural resource issues. No coding or programming is required.
